messages:
sophie_support: Heads-up — new hire @alex_newhire can't create a project even though they show as Org Admin in the console.
alex_newhire: Yes — when I click 'Create project' the button is grayed and the tooltip says 'insufficient permissions'. Trying via API returns 403.
josh_devex: Can you paste the curl you ran and the exact 403 body? Also which org and project context are you in?
sophie_support: curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk.redux-test\" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"acme-test"}'
response: 403 {"error":"permission_denied","message":"create_project: requires org.admin"}
org: acme-corp
alex_newhire: I was added to the org yesterday via SSO and I show role 'Org Admin' in the People page.
anna_platform: Quick checklist: repro via console? incognito? session stale? Also org-level policy could block project creation (billing/account mapping).
sophie_support: Repro in incognito still greys out the button. Token I used is the same one copied from user profile (Developer API key). Alex doesn't have a separate billing role.
josh_devex: Does the People page show the role with the little shield icon (i.e., inherited vs direct)? Sometimes group-mapped admins are read-only if there's an inherited deny on a nested org.
alex_newhire: People page shows role: Org Admin (source: Okta Sync). No shield, just says 'From SSO group: acme-admins'.
anna_platform: Could be two possible causes: 1) Org policy 'restrict_project_creation' enabled (applies to non-billing admins) or 2) the user's SSO group is synced but missing the billing scope claim, which blocks create_project even if role displayed in UI.
sophie_support: How do we confirm the policy? I can't find an obvious toggle in the console.
anna_platform: I'll check org settings. Meanwhile can you try creating project via a live session using my token (I can test)? Also check the API response headers for X-Request-Id and the audit log entry.
sophie_support: Re-ran request with X-Request-Id captured: x-request-id: 01F8B9R2Z3
sophie_support: I also checked Audit -> Role Assignments: shows Alex added via SSO group membership at 2026-03-15T10:02Z.
josh_devex: If it's a claim-scope issue, the API will block create_project but UI might still show role because the role was applied but scoped capabilities were pruned. Can Alex paste the raw id_token claims (redact PII) or we can ask Okta team for the SAML/SCIM mapping.
alex_newhire: pasted id_token claims to DM with josh and anna.
auth-bot: SYSTEM: Org policy \"restrict_project_creation\" is enabled for acme-corp (enforced on non-billing owners).
anna_platform: That's the smoking gun — policy prevents non-billing admins from creating projects. Okta group gave Alex org.admin but not billing.owner scope. Two fixes: add Alex to billing owner group or temporarily grant a direct org-level billing scope, or disable the policy (not recommended).
sophie_support: Can we do a temporary workaround so Alex can proceed? They need to onboard a demo project today.
anna_platform: I can add Alex as billing.owner for 2 hours and we can roll back. I'll patch via admin API: POST /orgs/acme-corp/roles -> assign billing.owner to user: U-98321 (audit tracked).
sophie_support: Thanks. After anna's change Alex retried and can create project successfully.
alex_newhire: Confirmed — project created 🎉
josh_devex: Long-term: update SSO group mapping to include billing scope for acme-admins or create a separate acme-billing-admins group so admin role + billing scope come together. Also document that UI People page may show role but scoped policies can still deny certain actions.
sophie_support: I'll open a ticket with Okta contact to update SCIM mappings and add a KB note: '403 on project create despite Org Admin' referencing this thread and the policy name.
anna_platform: Filed internal ticket PLAT-7832 to persist a billing.owner mapping and recommended group changes. Tagging: #security #billing #idp.
sophie_support: Closing the support escalation — workaround applied, docs triaged. Ticket: SUP-2026-1092.
